About Us

A small studio built on design, not decoration.

We are a small digital design studio in Virginia. Everything in the shop is ours: made by us, or chosen by us and finished by us, and looked over once more before it goes up. New work arrives a little at a time.

Our story

Pixel & Print Studio is a studio of two people in Virginia, built on one belief: good design is not decoration, it is the feeling a thing gives you before you can explain why. We chase that feeling everywhere it hides. In light over a mountain ridge at dawn. In a mark simple enough to stitch on a chest and strong enough to remember. In a template that saves a small business owner an hour of dread.

What we make starts as a sketch, a color, a moment one of us could not shake, and it does not ship until it earns its place in our own daily lives. We stay small on purpose, and we drop new work every week, following curiosity across wallpapers, prints, apparel, and tools for people building things of their own.

Design for the daily bloom: small moments of beauty, made to be lived with.

What we make

Framed prints lead the work now. We paint the originals, then print and frame each one to order. That line carries Magnolia and Pine, a collection we made for one of our mothers, around Southern magnolia and pine, porch light, and moonlight. We make printable art sets under Paper & Pine, wallpaper singles, and the Blooming Duo pairs we compose for the iPhone Duo, so a scene blooms as the phone unfolds. Under Pine & Ember we make embroidered and printed apparel and the mark blanket, with scarves and a few pieces on Redbubble.

On The Planning Desk we keep the toolkits and planners together: planners, template packs, and email kits that give small business owners back some of the hours the unglamorous work eats. We publish books and journals through Amazon KDP. Our first paperback, the Haunted Chic Journal, is out, and a small line starts with a gratitude journal. Framed prints, apparel, and blankets sell through our Pine & Ember store on Printify. Digital work sells through Ko-fi and Gumroad, and the wallpaper singles live on Zedge. No stock bundles, no clip art.

The Pine & Ember mark

A pine does not beg the storm to pass. It stands in it. Roots down, head up, still there at daylight. That is the pine.

The crescent is fire that learned manners. Not a blaze that takes, an ember that keeps: heat held low and steady, the way a hearth holds a house, the way a window glows at the end of a long road because somebody is awake inside it.

Together they say one thing: I know where I am from, and it is still burning in me. Wear it like you mean it.
